context: Topological closure in an arbitrary topological space, two equivalent closed-superset presentations / intersection-of-closed-supersets
editorial_note: ProofWiki explicitly lists the intersection of all closed supersets (Definition 2) and the least closed containing subset (Definition 3) as equivalent topological closure characterizations. The intersection family is nonempty since the ambient X is closed, including X=empty; both formulations work without T1 or Hausdorff assumptions. Its other descriptions by derived sets and by boundary should not be silently conflated with separate definitions of the derived set, isolated points or boundary. The source's closure = A union boundary form is intentionally excluded from this admission to avoid a premature circular prerequisite when boundary is defined using closure. This context is not algebraic closure, integral closure, or field norm closure. Source sections: Definition 2, Definition 3, Definition 1 for distinction, Definition 4 excluded to avoid circularity
text: For a topological space (X,τ) and A⊆X, the closure cl_X(A) is the intersection of all τ-closed subsets F⊆X that contain A: cl_X(A)=⋂{F⊆X:A⊆F and X\F∈τ}.

text: For a subset A of a topological space X, its closure cl_X(A) is the smallest closed subset of X containing A (equivalently, the unique least element under inclusion of the family of closed supersets of A).

context: Boundary of a subset in an arbitrary topological space, equivalent closure/interior formulas / closure-minus-interior
editorial_note: ProofWiki's closure-minus-interior and intersection-of-closures-of-complements formulas are equivalent for every topological space, with no metric or separation axiom required. The ambient X is part of the object: boundary relative to a subspace can differ from boundary in a larger surrounding space. The page's additional 'closure and exterior' presentation says the boundary consists of points in A not interior or exterior, which fails for points of cl(A)\A and appears mathematically erroneous. Exclude and explicitly flag that formulation from intake instead of copying it or silently endorsing all source definitions. Also avoid using ambiguous overline A for complement: write X\A explicitly. Source sections: Definition from Closure and Interior, Definition from Intersection of Closure with Closure of Complement, Definition from Closure and Exterior excluded due to erroneous set containment
text: For a subset A of a topological space X, its boundary is ∂_X A=cl_X(A)\int_X(A), the points in the closure of A that are not interior to A.

text: Equivalently, for A⊆X in a topological space, the boundary is ∂_X A=cl_X(A)∩cl_X(X\A), where X\A is the complement relative to the given ambient X.

context: Kernel of an additive R-linear map between left R-modules / module-linear-map-zero-preimage
editorial_note: The direct ProofWiki linear-kernel page presents the zero-preimage definition in general R-modules and separately specializes to vector spaces, where it is also called null space. These are related but have different domain generality, so index as two contextual mathematical meanings grouped under kernel of linear transformation; do not treat arbitrary modules as field vector spaces, or kernels of generic nonadditive mappings as linear kernels. The zero of the CODOMAIN N (or W) is used; the kernel is a subset of the DOMAIN M (or V). Existing independently screened group-homomorphism kernel and categorical universal-property kernel remain distinct broader contexts and must not be overwritten. This page supplies no independent mathematical definition of linear transformation itself. Source sections: Definition for R-modules, In Vector Space, Also denoted as
text: Let φ:M→N be an R-linear map between left R-modules over the same associative ring R. The kernel is ker φ=φ⁻¹({0_N})={m∈M:φ(m)=0_N}, where 0_N is the identity of the additive group of N.

text: For vector spaces V,W over a common field K and a K-linear transformation T:V→W, its kernel (null space) is ker T={v∈V:T(v)=0_W}=T⁻¹({0_W}), the preimage of the zero vector in W.

context: Derivative function of a real function differentiable at every point of an open real interval / pointwise-derivatives-combined-into-function
editorial_note: ProofWiki differentiates a number f′(a) at a single interior point from the derivative function f′:I→R defined pointwise throughout an open interval on which f is differentiable. Its interval-level source explicitly assumes differentiability at every x, so the resulting derivative function has entire domain I; do not silently extend to functions differentiable only on a subset or to one-sided derivatives at endpoints. The preexisting independent OpenStax real derivative-at-an-interior-point source remains untouched; this candidate is a distinct but naturally linked function-valued object. Variable h must approach 0 through nonzero increments lying in the function domain. The notation y′ or d/dx does not create an additional mathematical meaning. Source sections: On an Open Interval, At a Point for relation only, With Respect To for notation only
text: Let I⊆ℝ be an open interval and f:I→ℝ differentiable at each x∈I. Its derivative function f′:I→ℝ is defined by f′(x)=lim_{h→0, h≠0}(f(x+h)−f(x))/h, with x+h∈I.
